## 2

I understand why some images can seem suspicious, especially when they come from agencies or media outlets people may not trust. But the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on a single photograph. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, see different stars from different latitudes, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, and track satellites and flights. Independent space agencies, universities, private companies, and amateur observers all produce consistent results. Those observations are much easier to explain with a spherical Earth than with a worldwide conspiracy involving millions of people.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules in the air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere. Much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches us, leaving more red, orange, and pink light— which is why sunsets can be so colorful.

## 4

雨下了一整夜，细密的水声敲打着窗玻璃，像有人在黑暗中轻轻叩门。街灯被雨幕揉成一团昏黄的光，空荡的路面映着屋檐和电线的倒影，偶尔有汽车驶过，溅起一片银亮的水花。远处的楼房沉默地立在雾气里，窗户零星亮着，仿佛每一盏灯后都藏着一个未眠的人。屋内很安静，只有钟表的滴答声和雨声交织在一起，让漫长的夜晚显得温柔而遥远。
